entries.title: HQ Exosuit
entries.body:
Six flyable suits: Sentinel, Strider, Bulwark, Abyss, Stratos and Flux.

Suit up at the Suit-Up Centre in your lobby (F on the plate, F at the kiosk to pick the frame, paint, finish and glow), or press U anywhere in the City to summon it; U again takes it off. Suited, Space takes off: W/S speed, A/D turn, Space/Shift up and down, hold X to boost, and it lands when you come down slow. Abyss dives under the sea; Stratos has no height cap. A visor HUD shows your flight. Everything is free, and other players see your suit.

Presence carries five small numbers while you wear it. No third-party assets.

entries.title: SkyStrike: wall crawl looks like a crawl, not flying
entries.body:
Upright spider cling on the face.

The wall pose used to tip the body nose-down like a dive, so crawling from the ground looked like floating or swimming above the surface. Crawl is now an upright crouch: chest into the wall, hips dropped, head up the climb, opposite limbs plant together. Idle is a static spider crouch; Shift runs with bigger, faster reaches. The body also pulls tighter onto the facade so the hands sit on it.

No new network calls - pose is local only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: SkyStrike: swing into a wall stays a swing
entries.body:
Crawl is ground-only.

Swinging, diving, or falling into a face used to start a wall crawl mid-air - that clung and broke the swing. Contact in the air now only stops you; a crawl starts when you walk into a building from the ground. Idle cling and slide still work after a ground grab; Space still kicks off.

No new network calls - collision is local only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: SkyStrike: stop floating when you walk past a building
entries.body:
No more auto-cling beside a tower.

Hopping or falling next to a facade used to latch a wall grip with no keys and slide you around the building. A grip now needs intent: walk into the face from the ground with a direction key, or already being inside the mass. After a deliberate grab, releasing keys still clings and slides down.

No new network calls - collision is local only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: SkyStrike: oriented city lots are solid again
entries.body:
No more sailing through rotated building corners.

Walk collision already used each lot's oriented footprint, but the air solids used the axis-aligned lot rect - the visual corners stuck out with nothing to hit. Air solids now use the same footprint, and the body stops on the oriented face rather than the fat bounding box.

No new network calls - collision is local geometry only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: SkyStrike: no more freeze mid-air, no more through the building
entries.body:
The stuck-in-air / through-the-building break, proven at runtime.

Wall cling no longer freezes you. With no keys on a face the body used to zero velocity forever - stuck in the dive silhouette half-inside the facade, unable to swing. Idle now slowly slides down the face. A fresh Shift press soft-pushes off and fires a web; Space still jumps away.

Intersecting a tower grabs and pushes out. A stalled swing or a dive that ends inside or against a face plants you on the contact plane and starts the crawl pose (dive cleared instantly), instead of hanging in the air.

No new network calls - collision and the pose are local only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: SkyStrike sticks, climbs, and looks the part
entries.body:
Three live-path bugs that made the city slinger feel broken, each proven at runtime.

No more mid-air wall latch. The grip used to grab a tower face from 6 m away (it returned a lead face even when nothing was in reach), drop it the next frame, and flicker wall to fall forever - that is why crawl and wall-run felt glitchy and why a dive into a building never stuck. The grip now only latches a face that is actually within reach, and a jump-away cooldown is honoured by the fall collision too.

Paper-thin facade panes no longer steal the crawl. Window decorations in the solid list passed a height check and confused the leave-probe; a crawlable wall must have real thickness. Diving into a stepped tower (podium + storey) sticks, climbs past the cornice onto the taller face, and never enters the mass.

The hero matches the concept sheet - matte charcoal suit, larger angular neon lenses, draped hood, sharp strike chest emblem with a soft glow rim, neon circuitry on the ribs.

No new network calls - collision and the pose are local only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: Crawl the wall: hands and feet on the face, not floating beside it
entries.body:
The wall crawl, proven at runtime on the live key to heading to grip to climb path.

Walking into a building and holding W starts the crawl on its own. You do not press Space to begin climbing - Space is the jump when you are on the ground. The grip used the camera heading, so a chase camera that had drifted sideways made W mean along the wall instead of into it, and the hero stood stiff beside the building. The grip now uses the body's own facing, which is the direction you walked in.

Once on the face the keys are wall-local. W climbs up, S climbs down, A and D crawl along it, no matter where the camera is. A sideways crawl used to slide down the face because gravity bled on every key press; it now only bleeds against an actual climb.

The grip turns the body to face the wall and holds it at contact distance, so the camera settles behind you and you climb the face instead of flying along it. The hold measures the gap along the grip's outward normal (never the nearest of four faces - on a wide podium that wrapped round to the far face and pulled the body across the building) and prefers the face that still rises above the head.

The grip does not drop you the frame it starts. The old release probe only reached 0.44 m into the wall, so a grip that started from a web zip's 1.25 m stand-off never found the surface and dropped the same frame - still floating in air beside the wall in the dive pose. The grip now holds while the gap along the normal is under 2.2 m and lets go only when the body is genuinely off the side.

A ledge mount never plants you inside a building. At a cornice the crawl steps up onto the low roof and onto the taller face behind it, landing outside that face at contact distance. The old step put the body inside the box, which is how it crossed a tower and came out the other side. Sweeps sample every 1.2 m, so a fast move cannot skip a thin solid.

A roof is ground, not a hover. The city's ground level is the street, so a body standing on a tower roof was never on ground - the air state kept it flying in the dive silhouette and the crest flickered between wall and fall as it slid along the top. A body resting on a solid top the city's ground level does not know about stands on it now, in the walk pose, with the feet on the roof instead of being snapped down to the street.

A crest is a walk-off, not a flicker. When a crawl tops out and no taller face stands in front, the body steps onto the roof and drops the grip - one top-out per roofline. The walk owns the body again the same frame.

The pose is a crawl, not a hover. The body is plastered to the face, head up to see the climb, and the hands and feet step in a diagonal crawl - one arm and the opposite leg reach, then the other pair. Shift plus a direction runs the face faster with longer reaches. A body near a wall with keys into it grabs it (free fall beside a face, and a web zip coming to rest 1.25 m short of its anchor); walking past a wall on the ground still does not snap onto it. Space off a wall jumps away and stays away.

No new network calls - collision, wall grips and the climb are local geometry and local physics only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: The city rebuilt: the Metro, the skyline and the parks
entries.body:
The city rebuilt. Walk-in Metro stations, a new skyline, and an amusement park in every v4 city.

No more teleports at stations. Walk down the stairs, or ride the lift between the street and the hall. Underground, the camera stays under the ceiling and inside the walls, so you see the station and not its roof. Vehicles cannot drive onto station entrances. The road tunnel and its cuttings have a 2 m footway each side, so you can walk through. The sea viaduct swings out to sea before turning, so its piers no longer stand on the island or its airport.

Commercial towers of 7 or more floors stand on a podium, and the tallest step in again near the top. About half the towers are dark-glass curtain walls; other offices get stone, brick and sandstone. New worlds rise toward downtown's core, up to 40 or more floors. Worlds from before v4 look as they did.

Every v4 city reserves 70 by 100 m of ground for the amusement park; where no park block is free the park is built there. Trees in the suburbs, campuses, civic and old-town land. Fast travel is gone from the travel menu. Every trip crosses the sea. The new worlds need the Arena redeployed.

No new network calls - the city is local geometry and local physics only.

entries.title: Jump off the HQ roof again, and a wall that runs instead of shakes
entries.body:
Four air-kit regressions, each proven at runtime on the live physics path.

Jump works on the HQ roof. The roof deck's solid top was 0.35 m above its walk height, so every resting body sat inside the slab, the collision pushed it down through the roof, and the jump's upward velocity was killed the moment it left. The deck solid's top is now the walk height, and a body standing on a thin floor is always pushed out the top, never down through it.

Wall contact runs instead of shaking. The old suction pushed into the face every frame and the collision pushed straight back, a ping-pong that read as stiff and glitchy. The grip now never adds speed into the face and only bleeds speed leaving it, so the crawl and the run move smoothly.

Space always jumps. Pressing Space while walking into a building on the ground used to start a wall grip and eat the jump; the jump now runs first. Space while gripped or near a wall jumps away into free fall instead of zipping into the face you are escaping. A wall genuinely in front at hand height still zips.

No new network calls - collision, wall grips and the jump are local geometry and local physics only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: City Gen v4 final: sound and settings, HQ spacing and tram desire lines
entries.body:
City Gen v4 final. The ambient slider and positional sound, HQ spacing, desire-line tram routes.

The Ambient sounds slider in Settings runs from 0 to 100% and scales thunder, rain, fireworks, jets, water, fountains, the city's hum and roadworks. Positional sound uses the inverse-distance model: full volume close up, quieter with distance, silent past each kind's maximum, panned left or right to where the sound is, with only the nearest few of each kind playing at once. Roadworks have their own sound. Bus and tram doors hiss open at their stops, and a tram rings its bell as it pulls away.

HQs are spread by a minimum gap of 40 m, front a local street or a collector only, and sit near a stop. Each HQ lot holds the tower, its garage, an apron and a driveway. HQs move to new lots after this update.

Tram routes follow desire lines instead of only running beside roads.

entries.title: No frozen swings, no auto re-aim, every building solid
entries.body:
The air kit's four open complaints, each proven at runtime on the live physics path.

A swing never hangs frozen. A rope fouled against geometry releases the line, and a body that covers no ground for half a second drops the line into free fall instead of parking in mid-air. A slow pendulum apex is a real swing and keeps the line.

The web stays on the building you attached to. Holding Shift no longer re-aims at a neighbouring tower; only a fresh press fires a new line.

Every building is opaque. The zip sweeps its whole move, and the airport's terminal, concourse, hangars, fire station, fuel farm, depot and car park join the solid list the swing, the zip and the fall already obey.

Running into a building sticks you to it. The contact face is the one the sweep ran into, and a direction key while walking into a face starts the grip on the ground: direction crawls, Shift and direction runs, Space jumps away into free fall.

entries.title: City Gen v4 phase 11: the graphics pass
entries.body:
City Gen v4 phase 11: the graphics pass. The streets and structures get their detail.

Roads get edge lines along the main roads, lane arrows before junctions, solid stop lines where a side street meets a main road, yellow box hatching at signalled junctions and chevrons where ramps split off. The City Line's boulevard has trees and clipped hedges down its median, and avenues have low shrubs.

Flyovers and the City Line viaduct get parapets with coping, expansion joints at every pier, pier caps on bearings, lamps along the decks and downlights underneath where a deck crosses a road. The tunnel gets proper light fittings and panelled walls, and the cuttings light up at night.

New frame budgets of 1,200 draw calls above ground and 240 below, guarded by a headless tour of eleven places in the city in CI and the release check. The busiest place draws 647.

entries.title: Swinging that slides, and a wall you can actually stick to
entries.body:
Four air-kit fixes, each proven at runtime on the live physics path.

Swinging is smooth. The body sweep keeps the full tangential travel and clips only the normal component on contact (it used to lose about a quarter of every frame's move, which read as a stutter), and the pump bonus ramps in at the bottom of the arc instead of switching on and off.

You cannot go through buildings. The rope clamp sweeps the pull path and stops at the last free point, the body is swept along its whole move rather than only checked at the destination, and a blocked clamp can only shorten the rope, never lengthen it.

Contact with a face sticks you to it. Hit a building while swinging or falling and you hold the face: a direction key crawls up/along/away it, Shift + direction runs it (faster climb and stride), and with no keys you just hang there.

Space jumps away from the building into free fall, from where W dives or Shift swings again.

entries.title: No more stuck swings, no more walking through towers, and a wall-run on every face
entries.body:
Four air-kit fixes, each proven at runtime on the live physics path.

You can no longer get stuck mid-swing. The body sweep now pushes out of any box the hero is already inside (a start inside a tower used to freeze him there forever), and the rope clamp can no longer snap the body through a building — a blocked clamp shortens the rope to the contact distance instead.

Swinging, zipping and free-falling are all swept against the city's solid geometry every frame, so a tower face stops you and kills only the speed into it.

Run into a building while swinging or falling and you run on the wall. The contact drops the rope and starts a wall-run: a direction key pointed into the face runs you up it, one along the face walks you sideways, Space kicks off (web zip if something is in front, else a wall-jump) and Shift swings off the face. The entry slam is spent on contact, so the run holds the face instead of sliding down it.

Not just buildings are opaque: tree crowns, roof decks, the park's rides and the bridges all report solid geometry now, so the web and the body meet them.

entries.title: A jump is a jump again, buildings are solid, and the web zip actually fires
entries.body:
Four fixes in the air kit, each proven at runtime.

A normal jump no longer looks like a dive. The glide shape (head and body down, legs up behind) used to be forced on every hop by the launch curl and the stretch weight. It is now driven only by how long you have actually been descending (and by W for a dive): a jump stays a jump, and the glide appears when you really fall. The dive itself is still the head-first swoop.

All construction is opaque. Swinging on a web, zipping to a point, or free-falling, you can no longer pass through a building. The body is swept against the city's solid AABBs every frame and stops at the face, with the speed into the wall killed so you slide along it.

The web zip is visible and it works. A wall in front of you, at hand height or below, used to be rejected as the street you just left, so Space found nothing and the web never drew. The anchor gate now accepts anything in front at any height (only the ground right under you is still refused), the aim fan reaches further sideways and down, and the line is drawn from the raised hand to the point.

Space in the air is never a silent no-op. It zips when there is something to grab, double-jumps when you still have a jump, and otherwise still kicks up and forward so the press is always visible.

No new network calls — collision, the zip and the pose are local geometry and local physics only. No third-party assets.

entries.title: The air kit, as a slinger: a fully-raised hand, straight-line release, a web zip, and a close camera on the ground
entries.body:
The web is a strand now, not a pipe: a thin bright core in a barely-there glow, so the neon reads as a line.

The web leaves a RAISED hand — and the arm goes COMPLETELY up, straight along the line, not forward-level. While you fire or hang on the web the shoulder aims at the anchor and the elbow is nearly straight, so the shot leaves a held-up palm and the hang reads as a real hang.

Releasing the web now COASTS in a straight line. You keep the speed you swung with and fly along the direction you let go on — no drift back toward the building the line was stuck to. Turning is a deliberate move: start another swing with Shift and you turn. That is also how you build speed — pump, release, coast, swing again.

Space in the air is a WEB ZIP. Fire a web at whatever is in front of you and get yanked to it, keeping the momentum so a zip chains straight into the next swing. With nothing to grab — open sky off the HQ top — the double jump still stands.

The camera has two stand-offs now. Standing and walking, it is close again the way it used to be. Only in the air does it pull back to the whole-body shot, so a swing is framed head to boots and a walk is framed like a walk.

The web is a strand, the railing holds you on the HQ deck (a jump leaves it), and a dive is a glide with the head down and the legs up behind.

No new network calls — the web, the zip, the coast and the camera are local geometry and local camera data only.

entries.title: More traffic lights
entries.body: Side streets get lights too: where a main road crosses a side street (a short green for the side street, so the main road barely waits) and at crossroads out of town, spaced at least 60 m apart and only where a waiting bus or tram has room. The Commons goes from 17 lights to 42.

entries.title: A sprint that reads as a sprint, SkyStrike's air kit, and Skyline Park is back
entries.body:
Walking is now the pace Shift used to give you (7 m/s, up from 4), and Shift runs at 10 m/s on a real human gait: the thigh lifts hard at contact and again through terminal swing, the hip drives back past the mid-line at toe-off, the knee folds for a heel-to-seat kick, and the arms swing a longer forward-biased arc at a sprint cadence. The forward bend is at the waist only, and it unwinds the moment you stop running.

SkyStrike opens the live Commons with its HQ towers and Skyline Park, and starts you on top of your own HQ rather than on the street — the hero is dropped on your roof deck, by its lift door, facing out. Helideck discs count, and the tallest neighbour is only the fallback. The teleport waits until the city has actually placed him and until the Arena's open-HQ list has settled: while Valley is open the page never polls that list itself, so the game pumps it and rebuilds the street when it lands. One teleport, then hands off — nothing watches him afterwards, so walking on the deck never gets yanked back to the spawn.

Fixed: the amusement park had gone missing from the live Commons. Nothing removed it. The 3.18 world generator ran the park lake and the metro through the park district, leaving one empty park block cut by a road down to a 32 m clear strip, and the park still asked for 56 m of clear ground. It found nothing to claim, so the Commons got its landmarks and no park at all. The gate is now the 28 m the rides actually need, and every ride is sized and placed against the fence rather than the strip's centre: on a narrow park the wheel gets smaller and the Carousel and Starswing decks tuck in, so nothing hangs over the fence. Skyline Park, its coaster and its rides are back on every live world, the Commons included.

Dive and web-swinging: Double Space is a double jump (the second kick spins you), and the way off the HQ deck — and the second jump is the taller of the two, so it actually clears the railing. A jump leaves the spot you stood on: the walk pace is the launch velocity and a standing jump kicks along the facing (it used to hop on the spot). The deck railing is clear of a jump — a jump leaves the roof free (3.22.2 makes walking itself stay on the deck). And in the sky the city is scenery: once your feet are off the surface, towers and street props no longer count as walls, so a web-swing can pass them. And the jump bend restores in the air: the curl unwinds in about a third of a second instead of holding until landing. W while falling from height dives head-first — arms back along the ribs, legs together, the camera tips down with you. Shift in the air fires a neon web out of the hand to whatever the city holds (a tower ledge, a streetlight, a bridge span), a sagging glowing line you can pump with WASD like a swing. Let go of Shift and the line drops that frame; Space while swinging kicks you up and forward. The body stretches, rolls and tucks in the air instead of hanging like a puppet. Fixed so this actually works in the city: the web now sticks to what the city is really made of (tower faces and ledges, every placed building, tree crowns and roof decks) instead of only door drums and signs, and the aim fan reaches sideways and down-forward, so a fall down a tower face finds an anchor; W while falling tips the whole body over head-first (root, spine and head), not just a waist bend; and free fall is a skydiver body — spine open, legs trailing, arms wide — never a standing forward bend. Calm turns the hop, spin and web off. No new network calls — the web is local geometry only.

entries.title: The City waits for a slow machine
entries.body: Entering the 3D City now allows 45 seconds to build it (was 15) before falling back to the classic City, so a slower computer gets the living City instead of the fallback.

entries.title: A city that lives
entries.body:
Built around the planned City Gen v4, never into it: everything reads the finished world through one adapter (games/citylife.js), so it works on today's worlds and on v4's the day it ships.

Every building has a use (homes, offices, warehouses, workshops) and a ground floor: shopfronts with awnings and signs, cafes with striped awnings, office lobbies, loading bays. Rooftops carry AC units, stair housings, antennas and water tanks. Windows light by use and hour — offices dark at night, homes lit in the evening, shops in opening hours.

Footpaths get benches, bins, bike racks, newsstands, food stalls and cafe tables. Residents work in the shops and cafes and lunch there; people sit on terraces, queue at stalls, wait at stops, gather at the school gate at 08:00 and 15:00, jog in the park, crowd the stadium on Saturdays, and parade on Sundays.

Traffic follows the hour (rush hours, quiet nights) and the place: taxis, vans, lorries, scooters and bikes. A street market on Wednesdays and Saturdays, roadworks on weekdays and Sunday's parade close their streets, the same for everyone.

entries.title: Big-city roads, and buildings that stay solid
entries.body:
The live City's streets (generator 3, the Commons and every personal island) are paved wider, each street at its own width: a 7.5 m two-lane side street, a 9.5 m street or an 11.5 m wide one, a 14.5 m four-lane avenue or a 17.5 m boulevard, with dashed lane lines between the lanes and traffic keeping to the kerb-side lane. Every lot, site and HQ stays where it was — the extra width comes off the front of the plots, a lot always keeping at least 60% of its ground, and a street that cannot have its width somewhere steps down there.

Driving is swept, not jumped: a fast car meets a wall, a trunk or a building's corner instead of landing inside it, a glancing hit slides along the wall, and a vehicle that ends up in a wall anyway is lifted back onto the road as soon as you try to drive it out (Back on the road).

entries.title: Sound that comes from somewhere
entries.body:
Every sound in the 3D worlds now comes from where it is. Traffic, other players' vehicles, trams, buses, trains, the metro, boats, helicopters, planes, doors, bells, the gondola, construction and fountains get louder as you get closer, fade with distance and pan left or right to where they are. Only the nearest few of each kind play at once, so busy streets stay clear.

Your own vehicle stays at full level while the camera rides with you, and fades when you leave it behind in photo mode, a fly-by or the Map.

A new Ambient sounds slider in Settings (0 to 100%) replaces the on/off switch and sets the level of weather, fireworks, jets, water and the city's hum. 0% is off, and if you had ambient sounds off they stay off.

entries.title: The transport revamp
entries.body:
Every city is at its highest level, so every line, stop, airport and building is open everywhere. Getting around is free: no fares, no day pass and no coins for buses, trams, the metro, trains, boats, Claude Cabs or helicopters.

New worlds (world generator version 3): every island and the Commons are laid out again with lakes, canals and a marina, and the transport is designed around them. Your HQ keeps its rank and is placed on the new layout; parked vehicles go home to their bay.

Real street trams with rails in the road and overhead wires, buses and trams you board and ride in a seat, a metro in real tunnels (M1 and M2, crossing at Central) with underground stations, the City Line railway, the Island Link train to the Commons from every island, a gondola, water buses, a lake launch, water taxis and boat hire. Commuters fill vehicles by time of day, and stops announce themselves.

Claude Cabs: ride (bike, hatchback, sedan, SUV, EV, helicopter or water taxi) or drive for a score, a rating and achievements. Call a helicopter to a helipad or an open area, and filter your own vehicles by cars, bikes and helicopters.

The phone (Backquote, or I in the City): Tickets with a journey planner, free tickets and airport check-in, live Departures, a Transit map with moving vehicles, Claude Cabs, Vehicles, the Dealership, Messages, Nearby chat, Phone calls, Camera, Gallery, Achievements, these Patch notes and Settings.

The live worlds moved to version 3 (claude-hq@3 and user:<id>@3); version 2 stays served for older clients.

Privacy: text messages, nearby chat and calls are new traffic between players through the Arena. Each carries only what you type, and each is opt-in to send (messages need your one-time opt-in; Nearby and Calls are switches in Settings); receiving can be blocked or muted. Photos never leave this computer.

entries.title: Grand Prix: every F1 circuit, and the 2026 grid in the dealership
entries.body: A new Valley game, Grand Prix, puts you on full-size F1 circuits: the 23 rounds of the 2026 calendar and 17 classics, each its own world at true length, built from the real centre lines of bacinger/f1-circuits (MIT). A time trial on Valley Rally's car physics: laps, three sectors, the delta to your best, a ghost of your best lap and a minimap. In the City, a Grand Prix Circuit (from tier 2) has a pit building, a start gantry and a grandstand; E under its arch picks a circuit and a car. The dealership adds a Formula 1 class with all 11 teams of 2026 in their team colours, free like the rest and drivable everywhere. Grand Prix is solo and sends nothing; the circuit data is bundled.

entries.title: Fireworks that crackle
entries.body: The show over the park fires about half as many shells, with room between bursts and a shorter finale. Each burst is a soft thump followed by the stars crackling as they fall, heard as if from far off.

entries.title: Mouse steering, a grenade launcher and a tank for four
entries.body: Mouse steering (a switch in the camera settings): click the view and the mouse turns you and the chase camera together; Esc gives the cursor back. A grenade launcher: on foot, X takes it out and F (or a captured click) lobs a grenade that bounces and goes off after 1.8 s, knocking back everyone within 6 m (Calm keeps you on the ground). A tank for four: K rolls your tank up, E drives it; the turret follows your camera and F fires a shell. Its three other seats are carpool seats: the first in becomes the gunner. The new presence fields (grenade, tank) are numbers only. Needs the Arena redeployed.

entries.title: Carpooling, pillion riders, and the Suzuki Access 125
entries.body: Beside someone driving in the City, E takes the next free seat: ride with them in a car, or hop on behind on a bicycle, a motorbike or a scooter. They drive and you go where they go; E gets you out. New in the dealership: the Suzuki Access 125, the first scooter, with seats for its rider and two behind. Presence carries whose vehicle and which seat only where the Arena lists "carpool". Also: a badly damaged car no longer pulls to one side by itself.

entries.title: Dragons and dinosaurs ride from day one
entries.body: Every dragon and the sea serpent now comes fully grown from adoption (any affection; the Arena's pets.rs stage_of and the page agree), and the big dinosaurs (T-Rex, Triceratops, Brachiosaurus, Stegosaurus) can be ridden straight away: walk up and press E. Affection still unlocks tricks. Needs the Arena release.

entries.title: Ride your pets
entries.body: A grown dragon (any of the seven), the grown sea serpent or a big dinosaur (Triceratops, Brachiosaurus, Stegosaurus, T-Rex, from the grown mark of 400 affection) that is out with you can be ridden in the 3D City: beside it, "E Ride <name>". You sit in a saddle on its back (added when it has none), the camera goes to a chase view behind and above, and the pet's own model carries you, big. Dragons fly (games/hqpetride.js, a slow, agile glider / helicopter hybrid): W / S set the speed it holds (25-45 m/s, S down to a hover with fast short beats), A / D turn and bank it, Space climbs with big beats (up to 8 m/s; on the ground a leap into the air), Shift descends (from a hover straight down, at speed a dive with the wings folded back, up to about 57 m/s), and with neither it glides on spread wings, sinking about 1 m/s. It lands anywhere flat, the HQ roof helipads with their landing assist included, and uses the helicopters' floors, ceiling (800 m), island-to-island flying on and Go to (N). E gets you off once landed or within 3 m of the ground. F breathes the dragon's element forward (fire, frost, lightning, prism, shadow wisps, gold glitter; visual only, none in Calm). Dinosaurs walk (W / S, Shift runs, their walk and run animations) and the serpent swims (on the water only). HUD hints, the ride pill and screen-reader tips say how. Multiplayer: a new presence code a = 13 (riding a pet; the first pet in pt is the mount, the height in h) behind the new petride capability; the Arena checks the mount can carry a rider (a grown dragon or serpent, a big dinosaur) and drops the frame otherwise. Others draw you on your pet, its wings and gait following your movement. Older Arenas: others see you on foot with your pet beside you. Needs an Arena deploy for others to see riders. Privacy: nothing new leaves the machine (the same pet numbers and name as 3.13's pt). Third-party assets: none new.

entries.title: Players are solid
entries.body: Other people in the City (and Mission Control) stop you as a wall does: a body on foot or on a board, the box of the bike, motorbike or car they ride or drive (turned their way; a car from the dealership at its own size), so you bump off them instead of walking or driving through. Not while they fly, nor someone on a floor above or below you. You can't push anyone, and one who walks into you can always be walked away from.

entries.title: Your pets stay with you, your lobby shows them, and the front door goes to the street
entries.body: Fixes: E in your lobby went to the nearest pet following you (always within 2 m) before any door, lift or ride, so using the front door said "Leave <name> here" and your pets were saved as staying home. Now E is a door's, a lift's or a ride's whenever one is there, and "Leave <name> here" / "Take <name> out" need you standing still, close (1.5 m to leave one, 2.2 m to take one out) and facing it. After a refresh the 3D HQ was often up before the Arena's capabilities, so your pets loaded from this browser's empty list and stayed gone (nobody following, nobody in the lobby) until you opened the Pets panel; they now load from the Arena as soon as it answers, and your stay-home pets appear in the lobby then. Out of your lobby's front door you came out on your roof: the 3.13.4 helideck overhangs your front door, and arriving counted as "above everything"; arriving now stands you at the spawn's own level (the street, or the deck for the roof lift). Tests: E priority (door before pet), facing and distance, lobby pets after a late list, the Arena reload, front gate to the street, lobby door destinations and triggers.

entries.title: A real helipad on your HQ, with your helicopter on it
entries.body: Every HQ tower's roof now carries a helideck: a steel deck raised 3 m over the top roof on legs and struts, cantilevered past it, a 9 m pad (7.5 m on the smallest lots: the pad stays over the lot) in its middle with a walkway and a low glass rail round it, so a helicopter's rotor fits with room to spare (it was a 2–3.6 m disc). The roof lift's head house, the crown (spire, antenna, domes, pagoda, deco, garden), the roof extras, the crew flag and the prestige beam moved out to the walkway's diagonals and rim, clear of the pad; the Art Deco parapet is low and under the deck. Your own pad has your helicopter parked on it: walk up from the roof lift, E to board, take off; land back and it stays; leave it elsewhere and a fresh one stands on your pad again after Return to HQ (T) or five minutes. Friends' pads stay free for landing. The landing assist eases the last metres till you are over the middle. Client-only.

entries.title: Pokémon sprites cached on your machine
entries.body: The HQ no longer hotlinks every sprite on every load: the page asks the local server (/api/sprite), which keeps each Showdown / pkparaiso / PokeAPI sprite in .sprite-cache/ in the HQ folder (gitignored, never committed: the art stays third-party), serves repeats from disk and only goes upstream on a miss. Strict allowlist (https, those four sprite libraries, no redirects; anything else is refused), images only (gif/png/webp, 2 MB max), upstream 404s remembered for a week, 200 MB cap with oldest-first eviction. The fallback chain is unchanged: a miss still ends at the generated monster sprite. Egress is the same sprite URLs as before, now sent by the server instead of the browser.

entries.title: HQ Studio previews live
entries.body: The Studio docks right, narrower, with one compact row of tabs, and the 3D view behind it frames what you edit left of the panel. Exterior: your actual tower (the City's own hqtower code) in a live 3D preview that stays pinned at the top while you scroll; it turns slowly (still in Calm), drag to orbit, wheel to zoom, Day/Night, Hide; every option rebuilds it (debounced) and glides the camera to what changed: the roof for crown and roof extras, the street for entrance, sign, flags and grounds, night for the night light. Lobby / Floors: the lobby or Mission Control is framed (you're taken there for now if you're elsewhere) and every click shows on it; close without Save and the saved look and your view come back. Layout: placing happens on the floor itself, seen from above: a translucent ghost of the item follows the pointer, green where it fits, red where it would overlap or run off the floor; click places, right-click or Delete removes, R turns, drag pans, scroll zooms; the item picker shows a small picture of each piece; the keyboard cursor still works. Also: the empty pill floating over the lobby (the pets prompt, created before it had anything to say) is gone.

entries.title: Solid traffic, true shapes; the boombox goes live
entries.body: What isn't a box no longer stops you as one: the stadium's oval bowl, the cooling tower, stacks and silos block their round outlines (not the square round them); you walk between a gantry crane's and the water tower's legs and step into a bus or tram shelter; the air base's control tower and radar are round and its parked jets block their own wings and tail, not a 10 x 16 m box; the airport car park's ground floor is open between its columns. The City's cars, buses and trams are solid: you hit them on foot, on a board and at the wheel (your car bumps off and dents, as off a wall) instead of passing through, only at your level (not the street under a bridge or a carpark deck), and they see your car at its size so they stop short of it. Live in the Music tab ("🔴 Go live") now puts the boombox on your shoulder in the City too, not only a Listen-room song. Anyone near you in the City listens to your live set (the same browser-to-browser stream as "🎧 Listen live", started for them when they walk up, louder the closer they are, stopped when they walk away). It never cuts over a Listen-room song they're tuned in to, a live set they chose in the Music tab, or their own. No new presence field: who is live comes from the room, as before.

entries.title: Tuning shop, pets and the HQ revamp
entries.body:
One release, one Arena deploy (migrations 0020, 0021 and 0022; presence capabilities tuning, pets and hqstyle).

The Tuning shop. Redline Tuning, a workshop next to the dealership in every city from tier 2 (Go to → Tuning shop; E at its bay), and Tune on any B1 row of the garage manager. Paint any catalogue or custom colour in gloss, matte, metallic, pearl or chrome, with a two-tone roof, stripes or a livery. Wheels: six rim designs per car or bike, rim colour, and a size step (the tyre's outside never changes). Window tint, a lip, ducktail or GT wing, and sport, quad or titanium exhausts (bikes: slip-on, under-seat, end can) that change the engine note. A number plate of your own (8 characters, filtered; your HQ's name stays the default). Live preview on a turntable under a lift with an orbit camera; B1 plinths and the City show your tuned vehicles. Free. Your owned vehicles' tunes are kept in the Arena (migration 0020, /v1/vehicles/:id/tuning) and other players see them through presence vt (the new tuning capability). Your starters' tunes stay in this browser. Needs the Arena release.

Pets. Adopt dogs (Shiba, Golden Retriever, Corgi, Husky, Dachshund), cats (Tabby, Siamese, Maine Coon, Black cat), dinosaurs (T-Rex pup, Triceratops, Raptor, Brachiosaurus baby, Stegosaurus), dragons (Wyvern, Fire, Ice, Storm, Crystal, Shadow, Golden) and a Sea serpent at Paws & Claws, the City's new Pet shop (Go to: Pet shop), or from the Pets panel (Cmd-K, Settings). Dogs and cats are free; rarer pets are free from their HQ level or sooner for Poke Coins. Up to 6, two out with you. They follow you round the HQ, B1 and the City, go round buildings, catch up if left behind, idle, nap, hop in your car, fly beside your plane or swim beside your boat. B throws a ball to fetch, U pets, O does a trick (more unlock with affection), and dragons grow. Each dragon has its element: frost breath and snow, fire and embers, lightning, prism sparkles, shadow wisps, gold glitter (off in Calm). The rest live in your HQ lobby, roam, nap and greet you; E takes one out or leaves one there, and visitors to your open HQ see them. Friends see your pets through the new "pets" presence capability (species, colours, accessories, growth and name, at most two). Older Arenas keep pets in this browser only. Privacy: pet names you type go to the Arena (checked and word-filtered). Pets look and move like animals: rounded bodies, eyes that blink, jointed legs that walk, trot and gallop, wagging tails, flicking ears, sit and sleep poses, and dragons with folding membrane wings that flap and glide; the Shiba, Husky, Golden Retriever and the dinosaurs use animated low-poly models (the rest stay procedural). Backend: migration 0022_pets.sql and /v1/pets/* (deploy needed). Third-party assets: CC0 animated models by Quaternius (Ultimate Animated Animals: Shiba Inu, Husky; Animated Dinosaurs: T-Rex, Velociraptor, Triceratops, Stegosaurus, Apatosaurus) in games/pets/ with LICENSE-quaternius.txt, served only from 127.0.0.1.

The HQ revamp and HQ Studio. Every HQ is grander and a bit bigger, as far as its lot allows: a podium with a grand entrance, setback tiers, six facade systems, lit signage and night lighting, crowns, roof extras and landscaping, and a working helipad on every roof. Land a helicopter on any HQ, get out, walk the roof deck and take the roof lift down; the Lobby has a Roof lift up. HQ Studio (Settings, Cmd-K or the lobby kiosk) styles your tower, a new double-height lobby (reception, centrepiece, seating, art, rugs, signage, ambience), each floor's walls, floor, lighting and furniture, and lets you place decor and pet furniture on a grid. Others see your style when the Arena supports it (migration 0021, "hqstyle"); otherwise it stays on this machine. Privacy: only the style document (enums, colours, grid cells) goes to the Arena, nothing from transcripts. Third-party assets: none. Needs an Arena deploy.

entries.title: Driving feel + convoys
entries.body: Cars, motorbikes and bicycles in the City (games/hqdrive.js): lights switch on at night and in heavy rain, a storm, snow or fog (L toggles them by hand), brighter lamps and tails plus one additive pool-and-cone mesh on the road (no real lights, one draw call per lit vehicle); other players' vehicles light up from your own clock and weather. Grip: rain, storms and snow lower lateral grip and braking (about −35 % braking in a storm, −50 % in snow; two wheels lose more and ride slower), powerslides come easier and last longer, and wet-road spray flies off your wheels (off in Calm); the drive HUD shows Wet road / Snow, the lights and the damage. Damage: hits above ~22 km/h dent the panels you hit, crack a headlight and, past 70 %, smoke from the bonnet (not in Calm); a wrecked car pulls slightly. Cosmetic, kept per vehicle in localStorage; the garage kiosk, the B1 car lift and the dealership repair it. Convoys: Y invites the nearest player within 40 m (or 🚗 Convoy in Here now), Y accepts or leaves, hold J for a soft assist that steers and throttles you into your slot (behind-left / behind-right on the road, a wider echelon in the air), a convoy panel lists members, distances and "In formation", and the leader's Go to destination is shown to every follower. You leave on a world change or past 300 m. The Arena relays it with presence (ci / cv / cg, the new "convoy" capability); older Arenas hide convoys. Privacy / egress: user ids of the people you invite / follow and your Go to point ride City presence, only where the Arena lists "convoy". Third-party assets: none. Backend: backend/ changed (deploy needed).
